nodes.name: Section — 🚀 Release — reaction on a post or a Posty DM

parameters.content:
## 🚀 Release — reaction on a post or a Posty DM
Resolve Release decides: POST (repost to #releaseme, mark RELEASED, confirm), PARK (not indexed yet → pending) or DROP (already released, not the poster, Studio M, …, and says why). Only the poster, or a release admin (Tara), can release. When Tara releases someone else's project, Tell Poster DMs the engineer.

## New project posted in #newpostprojects
Writes the index row and DMs the poster the project (that DM is its notify_ts, so a 🚀 on it releases). A QU that is already in use gets a thread reply instead. Then the post goes straight to the Xero typo check (Workflow 5), without waiting.

## DM → "my open projects"
Any other DM to Posty. Sends the person one message per open project and records each message ts as notify_ts.

## Intake post deleted
Marks the row DELETED so a re-post registers as new instead of an unreleasable duplicate.

## Undo — Posty's #releaseme post deleted
Deleting the repost undoes a mistaken release: the row goes back to OPEN.

## Manual release typed in #releaseme
Nudges the person to react 🚀 on the post instead. The hourly refresh still records it.

## Leadership commands — digest, refresh
"digest" (leadership + Joaquin) runs Workflow 3 for the asker only. "refresh" (Tara, Joaquin) rewrites every Tracker canvas now.

## Tara commands — typos, remind
"typos" runs the Xero typo check as a preview (DM only). "remind <name>" sends that engineer their open list.

## Shared — ack cleanup + errors
Clear Ack removes the 👀 once a DM is handled. Notify Error tells the person something went wrong, and Alert Tara DMs Tara the details.

## Posty — Events Endpoint

One Slack app = one Request URL, so every event lands
here and `Classify Event` routes it.

### Four flows
1. **NEW_PROJECT** — a QU post in #newpostprojects.
   Indexes it immediately, DMs the poster
   "You started …", records the DM as `notify_ts`.
2. **RELEASE** — 🚀 on the intake post OR on a DM
   Posty sent. Resolves via `source_ts` then
   `notify_ts`. Reposts verbatim, marks released,
   DMs the releaser.
3. **LIST_REQUEST** — any DM to Posty returns that
   person's open projects, oldest first, capped at
   25. One message each so they can be rocketed.
4. **IGNORE** — everything else, including Posty's
   own messages, joins, deletions and un-reactions.

### ⚠️ TARGET CHANNEL IS STILL A TEST TARGET
`Post Release` posts to **U026N6E1R** (tara's DM),
not #releaseme. §14.9 — a bug here puts junk in
front of Accounting.
**To go live:** set Channel on `Post Release` to
`CC9EG3K8C`. One field.

### Why indexing happens on post
The nightly refresh used to be the only way a row
appeared, so a rocket minutes after posting always
landed in PENDING. Indexing on the message event
makes PENDING rare — it now means n8n was down
when the post happened.

### Logic lives in code/
resolve-release.js, and the classifier mirrored in
scripts/test-classify. Edit there, run the tests,
paste back. Never edit only a node.

### Attribution
`Post Release` appends "Released by @person" on a
second line. Every post in #releaseme now comes
from Posty, so without it the channel loses the
author information it used to carry. The verbatim
first line is untouched.

### Why `Not From Posty` sits first
Every message Posty sends comes back as an
event. That was ~90% of all executions, and each
one paid the Code-node cold start — up to 3.6s.
Slack retries after 3s, so slow runs were
producing DUPLICATE event deliveries.

A Filter node runs in ~2ms and needs no task
runner, so dropping bot messages before
`Classify Event` removes the cold start from the
vast majority of events.

`Classify Event` still checks bot_id itself —
this gate is an optimisation, not the guard.
